## What happened

In the last 187 days: 15,843 purchase events against 12,973 in the 187 days before (+22%, a clear change), total value 5,530,641 (+38%). 5,881 customers were active (3,867 seen for the first time in this data); 3,731 active before were not.

## Predictions

- Windows tried: 30 days, 60 days, 90 days; each must pass the gate at 96.7% confidence, corrected for trying 3.
- A model to predict whether purchase happens within 30 days was promoted. On 1,803 held-out entities the model ranks outcomes with AUC 0.881, against 0.776 for the baseline rule. At 97% confidence the gain is between +0.092 and +0.121 (AUC). It was also checked in 3 segments (history length) and is not clearly worse than the baseline rule in any of them. None of the 12 candidate inputs the search tried improved it.
- A model to predict whether purchase happens within 60 days was promoted. On 1,622 held-out entities the model ranks outcomes with AUC 0.888, against 0.750 for the baseline rule. At 97% confidence the gain is between +0.125 and +0.153 (AUC). It was also checked in 3 segments (history length) and is not clearly worse than the baseline rule in any of them. None of the 12 candidate inputs the search tried improved it.
- A model to predict whether purchase happens within 90 days was promoted. On 1,487 held-out entities the model ranks outcomes with AUC 0.890, against 0.708 for the baseline rule. At 97% confidence the gain is between +0.163 and +0.199 (AUC). It was also checked in 3 segments (history length) and is not clearly worse than the baseline rule in any of them. None of the 12 candidate inputs the search tried improved it.
- The model to predict the value of the next purchase was not promoted. On 487 held-out entities its average error is 254.73, against 239.82 for the baseline rule. At 90% confidence the gain is between -0.113 and -0.017 (relative error reduction). It does not lower the baseline rule's error, shows no clear gain, since that range includes zero and is clearly worse than the baseline rule for entities with more than 5 records (139 held-out entities), so the current model or rule stays in use. None of the 12 candidate inputs the search tried improved it.
